title: Roof Brackets: Use Locking Brackets and Real Fall Protection
summary: A carpenter died after a roof bracket folded flat when he reached for a plank, and he fell about 19 feet. The adjustable brackets had no locks and were not used with other fall protection. Use locking brackets, follow the maker's spacing, and tie off.
talking_points: A carpenter climbed onto a roof to get a plank from a bracket scaffold. When the plank bounced, the bracket's arm lifted out of its notch and the bracket folded flat. He fell about 19 feet and died.
Fall protection is required at 6 feet or more in residential construction. Use conventional fall protection: a guardrail system, a safety net, or a personal fall arrest system.
OSHA does not count roof brackets as conventional fall protection. In most cases use them only together with guardrails or a personal fall arrest system.
A personal fall arrest system needs a full-body harness, a connector, and an anchor that holds at least 5,000 pounds or twice the intended load. A body belt is not allowed for fall arrest.
Guardrail top rails are 39 to 45 inches high and must hold 200 pounds. Midrails sit halfway between the top rail and the surface. On a new house, install guardrails early and leave them in place.
Do not use adjustable roof brackets that have no locking mechanism. Use brackets that lock the support arm into the base, or fixed brackets.
Follow the manufacturer's instructions. These brackets were spaced about 12 feet apart, and most makers call for closer spacing.
Employers must have a safety and health program that covers fall prevention and spotting unsafe conditions, with training for every worker.
site_hazards_to_check: Adjustable roof brackets with no locking mechanism
Bracket spacing wider than the manufacturer allows
Planks that bounce, shift, or are not secured
No guardrail, safety net, or personal fall arrest system at the roof edge
Workers climbing onto a roof only to retrieve materials with no tie-off
discussion_questions: What type of fall protection do we have at the roof edge today?
Do our roof brackets lock, and are they spaced as the maker requires?
Where is the anchor point for each person who goes on this roof?
